title: Adaptive micro-router for speculative decoding with kernel fingerprinting and confidence gating
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Goal: Build an adaptive micro-router that performs lightweight model/kernel fingerprinting at prefill time and applies token-level confidence gating during decode to decide when to accept speculative chunks or fall back to slower, higher-fidelity model variants. This ticket covers design, telemetry, and a staged canary rollout for runtime-side speculative decode support. The approach prioritizes predictable latency SLOs while recovering quality via deterministic fallbacks and KV-cache-aware warmup when acceptance thresholds fail.
background: Current speculative-decode work focuses on candidate scoring and staged fallback, but lacks fine-grained kernel-aware routing and an operational acceptance signal that ties directly to served latency/cost budgets. Operators have asked for per-request justification and opt-out hooks so we can reason about emergent regressions and provide safe fallbacks for enterprise customers with strict SLAs.
proposal: 1) Kernel fingerprinting: during model load and fast prefill probe, compute a compact fingerprint (architecture, quantization profile, preferred kernel set, sequence-length profile) and attach to request metadata. 2) Micro-router policy: evaluate fingerprint + request constraints (max latency, cost tier, region) to select either: a) primary speculative path (fast kernels, smaller model variant), b) buffered speculative (prefill-only parallel probe), or c) direct conservative path (full model). 3) Confidence gating: during decode, compute token-level acceptance metric (delta-NLL + top-logit margin + token-entropy heuristic) on candidate chunk; accept if metric < threshold. Threshold is adaptive: initially calibrated offline per-model, then adjusted on live traffic using a feedback controller that targets a configured downstream QA metric and latency budget. 4) Fallback: when gating rejects, route remaining output to conservative path with KV cache warmup and deterministic re-decode; preserve earliest accepted tokens and emit a single merged response to the client with a confidence flag. 5) Observability: emit per-request reason codes, acceptance score, selected kernel fingerprint, and fallback events to Console for alerting and regression detection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Micro-router can attach a kernel fingerprint to 100% of prefill requests with <1ms overhead in the fast-path.
- Token-level acceptance score computed and logged for speculative chunks; weekly aggregate shows stable distribution compared to offline baseline.
- Fallback path incurs median extra latency <= 2x of baseline conservative decode on Canary targets.
- No customer-facing quality regressions in canary cohort measured by automated eval prompts (pass rate >= 98% of baseline).
- Per-request reason codes and telemetry viewable in Console; alerts trigger when acceptance-rate drops >10% for 1h.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit tests + integration tests with synthetic workloads and kernel-variant matrix. Phase 1 (internal canary): 1% internal traffic, debug logs enabled, blocked for 48h review. Phase 2 (external canary): 5% of non-SLA production traffic for 1 week, lightweight alerting. Phase 3 (gradual ramp): increment to 25% over 2 weeks with automated rollback on regressions. Enterprise tenants pinned to conservative path unless opted in.
telemetry_and_metrics:
- per_request.kernel_fingerprint: string tag
- per_request.acceptance_score: float
- per_request.accepted_chunks: int
- per_request.fallback_triggered: bool
- latency.p50/p95 for speculative vs conservative paths
- cost.per_token comparison
- quality.regressions measured by eval harness (daily)
- reason_code histogram for routing decisions
- kernel_hotness counters to track frequently selected kernels
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: acceptance metric miscalibration could silently degrade quality. Mitigation: conservative initial thresholds, canary evals, automatic rollback.
Risk: kernel fingerprinting misclassifies models leading to suboptimal kernel selection. Mitigation: fall back to architecture-level default kernels and include kernel-selection explanation in logs for debugging.
Risk: KV cache warmup increases tail latency. Mitigation: preload caches proactively when micro-router predicts probable fallback using short-run prefill probes.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- We choose compact fingerprinting over heavy profiling to keep prefill overhead low (trade: less granular kernel selection vs performance).
- Adaptive thresholds trade simplicity for robustness; controller complexity justified by improved cost/quality balance on heterogeneous workloads.
- Merge-on-fallback (single response) chosen to keep API stable; alternative multi-response mode planned as later opt-in.
open_questions: What is the canonical format for kernel fingerprints across runtime and model onboarding?
Should enterprise customers get an opt-in to receive deduplicated fallback traces?
How aggressive should the feedback controller be when acceptance signal drifts during peak load?
